display: A benrishi (Japanese trademark and patent attorney) in Tokyo who handles Japanese trademark filings and oppositions for small Chinese manufacturers, working in Mandarin.

signals.text: I'm drafting a trademark opposition and need certified Chinese-to-Japanese translations of invoices and catalogue pages as evidence. I'm looking for a fast, reliable quote.
I have a trademark opposition with a hard JPO deadline in mid-November. The main difficulty is proving prior use in China, because the JPO prefers use in Japan.

I want to write a twenty-page simplified Chinese guide, 'Five mistakes Chinese factories make when registering a mark in Japan'. I have the outline and three case studies but no time to write the second half.
I'm looking for a Japanese-Chinese translator who understands the difference between patent-law and trademark-law terms. One wrong term in an office action can cost a client a month.
More small Chinese makers are quietly expanding into Japan this year, partly because the US market looks risky. My inquiries are rising while other China-related business seems quiet.
A toy manufacturer in Shantou has asked about filing in classes 28 and 35. I'd like to meet more makers in toys, consumer goods and small appliances.
Cross-border referrals are active: a Shenzhen lawyer is sending an LED-strip client who wants a Japanese registration.
Clients often ask me to rule on brand names that sound like Japanese words, and some names carry deep personal meaning for the owner. I want better ways to help them choose a new name.
I'm stretched thin between client calls late in the evening, drafting, and the writing project. I would welcome help with the guide.
I'm training for the Tokyo Marathon lottery along the Sumida River and enjoy running with others. I'd also happily talk fountain pens.
I'll be away from the office for a few days around 10 October, and I can't travel to China before December.

offers.text: Registered benrishi with eleven years of experience, independent for three years, handling Japanese trademark searches, filings, oppositions and JPO office-action responses.
I negotiate and advise in Mandarin, with documents in Japanese. I studied law at Peking University for two years.
Bilingual templates for trademark search reports, JPO office-action responses and opposition notices.
A small Kanda office with a paralegal and a part-time Japanese-Chinese translator, able to handle document logistics for Chinese clients.
Working relationships with law firms in Shenzhen and Hangzhou, so I can pass on and receive cross-border referrals.
I explain how Japanese examiners judge phonetic similarity, distinctiveness and prior use, in plain Mandarin that a factory owner can follow.
Practical knowledge of how small Chinese manufacturers sequence a Japan entry: classes, timing, and what the JPO will and won't accept as evidence.

catchers.hypo: I'm a lawyer in Guangzhou. My client makes home appliances and wants to register their brand in Japan. Do you take referrals from Chinese firms?
catchers.can: I run a search first, then file and handle the JPO side in Mandarin. I can work as the Japan counterpart to the referring firm, as I already do with firms in Shenzhen and Hangzhou.
catchers.confirm: Is the matter a trademark or patent filing or dispute in Japan, rather than general corporate or contract work?

catchers.hypo: My factory's brand name sounds like a Japanese word and I'm afraid it will be rejected, but the name matters a great deal to me. What can I do?
catchers.can: I check the phonetic and conceptual conflicts against the Japanese register, then explain realistic options: keep the name with adjustments, file a variant, or add a separate Japanese-market mark.
catchers.confirm: Is the issue a trademark name that might be refused in Japan, rather than a trademark dispute in another country?

catchers.hypo: A Japanese distributor registered a mark almost identical to ours in the same class. Our brand has been used in China for years, but we have never sold in Japan. Can we oppose?
catchers.can: I assess the opposition grounds and how to present Chinese prior-use evidence to the JPO. I also state plainly where it is weak.
catchers.confirm: Is the other party's mark published within the JPO opposition period, and do you have invoices or catalogues proving use before their filing date?

catchers.hypo: I translate Japanese legal documents into Chinese, including IP material, and I'm looking for steady work with a patent attorney.
catchers.can: I can test translators on trademark office-action terminology and pass work to a reliable one through my office.
catchers.confirm: Do you have direct experience translating JPO office actions or trademark documents, not only patent specifications?

catchers.hypo: I'm a Chinese-speaking law graduate who wants to understand how a Japanese IP office works. Could I learn from a paralegal there?
catchers.can: My paralegal Sato studied Chinese and works inside the office. I can introduce a short exchange or an informational chat if it suits both sides.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for a short learning conversation or an introduction, not a paid job placement?

catchers.hypo: I edit business content for Chinese SMEs. I can proofread or co-write a practical guide on registering marks in Japan.
catchers.can: I can share my outline and three case studies and review the Chinese text for legal accuracy.
catchers.confirm: Do you write plain simplified Chinese for factory owners and can you work from a lawyer's outline, rather than do only light copy-editing?

catchers.hypo: I run a Japanese company that wants to distribute a Chinese product. Can you check whether the Chinese brand can be registered here first?
catchers.can: I run a trademark search and tell them what is already registered in the relevant classes. I can only act for the party who hires me, and I check for conflicts first.
catchers.confirm: Does your side want to secure the mark for a Chinese brand owner, rather than register a mark that conflicts with one the owner already filed?

forbids.text: I only take trademark and patent work. No contracts, corporate, litigation outside IP, or other legal fields.
I use a fixed hourly rate and don't discount for new clients.
I can't travel to China before December.
I won't treat a fee negotiation at the start as a harmless detail, because it tends to repeat at every invoice.

projects.name: Five mistakes Chinese factories make when registering a mark in Japan
projects.text: A twenty-page simplified Chinese guide for small manufacturers. The outline and three case studies are done, and a Shenzhen lawyer has offered to proofread. The second half still needs drafting.
roles_needed: Case-study contributor from a Chinese factory

policy.t1: When there's a real signal, I share typical cases, fee level, the process, and the client sectors I handle.
policy.t2: Once the match is strong and the other side's identity is clear, I talk about pricing flexibility and how I handle difficult client situations.
policy.never: My father's illness and my personal finances.
